title: A-Level Chemistry
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 7 in GCSE Chemistry (or 7-7 in Combined Science) plus Grade 6 in GCSE Mathematics and Grade 5 in English Language.
description: A-Level Chemistry delves into the fundamental building blocks of the physical universe. Students study physical chemistry, inorganic periodicity, and organic synthesis, supported by over 100 hours of university-standard laboratory practical work in our modern laboratories.

teacher.name: Dr. Alistair Finch
teacher.credentials: PhD in Chemical Biology (Imperial College London), FRSC

assessmentMethod: Three terminal written examinations (2 hours each) at the end of Year 13, plus practical endorsement certificate.

title: A-Level Physics
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 7 in GCSE Physics (or 7-7 Combined) and Grade 7 in GCSE Mathematics. Concurrent study of A-Level Mathematics strongly recommended.
description: From subatomic particle physics to cosmic astrophysics, A-Level Physics explores nature's deepest governing laws. Students develop advanced mathematical modelling and laboratory investigative skills using digital oscilloscopes, laser interferometers, and computerized sensors.
assessmentMethod: Three written exam papers (Modelling Physics, Exploring Physics, Unified Physics) plus Practical Endorsement.

title: GCSE Biology (Higher Tier)
entryRequirements: Satisfactory completion of Key Stage 3 Science with strong aptitude in scientific inquiry and mathematics.
description: GCSE Biology delivers an engaging journey into living organisms, covering cell biology, human physiology, genetics, biotechnology, and ecosystem dynamics with intensive microscopy and ecological field work.
assessmentMethod: Two 1 hour 45 minute written papers covering core theory and required practical techniques.

title: A-Level Mathematics
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 7 in GCSE Mathematics. An entrance diagnostic test is conducted during induction.
description: Considered the gold standard for university readiness, A-Level Mathematics combines pure mathematical rigor (calculus, trigonometry, algebra) with applied mechanics and real-world statistics data interpretation.

teacher.name: Mr. David Pembroke
teacher.credentials: MA Mathematics (University of Cambridge, First Class)

assessmentMethod: Three 2-hour written exam papers: Pure Mathematics 1, Pure Mathematics 2, and Applied Statistics & Mechanics.
keyTopics: Statistical Hypothesis Testing & Large Data Sets

title: A-Level Further Mathematics
description: An intensive, elite course designed for aspiring mathematicians, computer scientists, and engineers. Covers advanced pure mathematics including complex numbers, matrices, hyperbolic functions, and polar coordinates.
assessmentMethod: Four 90-minute papers: Core Pure 1, Core Pure 2, Further Pure 1, and Further Mechanics 1.

title: A-Level Computer Science
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 6 in GCSE Mathematics and Grade 6 in GCSE Computer Science (or demonstrated coding portfolio in Python/Java).
description: Prepares students for modern software engineering and computational research. Covers computer systems, processor architecture, computational algorithms, complexity theory, and a significant independent non-exam software project.

teacher.name: Ms. Priya Patel
teacher.credentials: MSc Software Engineering (UCL), BEng Computer Science

assessmentMethod: Paper 1 (40%), Paper 2 (40%), and an independently coded NEA Programming Project (20%).
keyTopics: Data Structures, Trees, Graphs & Hash Tables

title: BTEC National Extended Diploma in Information Technology
entryRequirements: 5 GCSEs at grade 4 or above, including GCSE English Language and Mathematics.
description: A comprehensive vocational qualification offering practical mastery in relational database design, cloud computing, cybersecurity architecture, website development, and IT systems project management.

teacher.name: Mr. Samuel O'Connor
teacher.credentials: BSc Information Systems (King's College London), CISSP

assessmentMethod: Mix of externally marked exams, controlled computer assessments, and internally verified portfolio assignments.

title: A-Level History
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 6 in GCSE History and Grade 6 in GCSE English Language or Literature.
description: Cultivates analytical precision, critical documentary analysis, and persuasive argumentation through deep explorations of the British Stuart Monarchy and 20th-century Russian Revolution to Cold War.

teacher.name: Dr. Helena Montgomery
teacher.credentials: MA, PhD History (LSE), Fellow of the Historical Association

assessmentMethod: Two 2.5-hour written papers (80% total) and an independently researched 4,500-word historical investigation (20%).
keyTopics: The Tudors & Stuarts: Crown, Government & Crisis

title: A-Level Economics
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 6 in GCSE Mathematics and Grade 6 in GCSE English Language.
description: Examines how societies allocate scarce resources, the functioning of competitive markets, market failure interventions, and macroeconomic policy across inflation, fiscal stimulus, exchange rates, and international trade.

teacher.name: Mr. Jonathan Hayes
teacher.credentials: MSc Financial Economics (LSE), Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)

assessmentMethod: Three 2-hour papers: Markets and Business Behaviour, The National and Global Economy, and Micro & Macro Synoptic.
keyTopics: Market Mechanisms, Price Elasticity & Market Failure
Monetary and Fiscal Policies & Bank of England Actions
Emerging Markets, Global Trade & Financial Systems

title: BTEC Level 3 National Extended Certificate in Business
entryRequirements: 5 GCSEs at grade 4 or higher, including English Language and Mathematics.
description: An applied qualification focused on enterprise, corporate finance, digital marketing campaigns, and international business management. Features live case studies and partnerships with London business mentors.

teacher.name: Mrs. Karen Bradley
teacher.credentials: MBA (London Business School), BA Business Management

assessmentMethod: Four units: Exploring Business, Developing a Marketing Campaign (Controlled Assessment), Personal and Business Finance (Exam), and Recruitment Selection.

title: A-Level English Literature
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 6 in GCSE English Literature and GCSE English Language.
description: An inspiring critical examination of drama, poetry, and prose across five centuries. Students explore Shakespeare, Gothic fiction, romantic poetry, and contemporary voices with close textual analysis and seminar debate.

teacher.name: Dr. Beatrice Rowe
teacher.credentials: MA English (King's College London), PhD Literary Studies (Exeter)

assessmentMethod: Two 2.5-hour written examinations (80%) and one 3,000-word comparative NEA essay (20%).
keyTopics: Shakespeare & Pre-1900 Drama: Hamlet and The Duchess of Malfi
The Gothic Genre: Dracula & The Bloody Chamber
Post-1900 Poetry and Close Critical Reading
Literary Theory: Feminist, Marxist & Postcolonial Readings

title: A-Level French
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 7 in GCSE French and Grade 6 in GCSE English Language.
description: Fosters bilingual fluency and deep cultural immersion into contemporary Francophone society, cinema, and literature. Features weekly one-to-one native speaker conversation coaching in our language lab.

teacher.name: Mme. Sylvie Dubois
teacher.credentials: Agrégation de Lettres Modernes (Sorbonne), MA Applied Linguistics

assessmentMethod: Paper 1: Listening, Reading and Translation (50%); Paper 2: Written Response to Film & Book (20%); Paper 3: Speaking Assessment & IRP (30%).
keyTopics: Current Trends in French Society & Family Structures
Artistic Culture & Heritage in the Francophone World
Immigration, Integration & The Extreme Right in France
Literature Study (Camus - L'Étranger) and Film Study (La Haine)

title: GCSE Spanish (Higher Tier)
entryRequirements: Prior study of Spanish in Key Stage 3 with good foundation in grammar and vocabulary.
description: Develops practical conversational competence, cultural understanding of Spain and Latin America, and solid grammatical foundation across listening, speaking, reading, and written expression.

teacher.name: Sr. Carlos Mendoza
teacher.credentials: Licenciado en Filología Hispánica (Universidad de Salamanca), QTS

assessmentMethod: Four equally weighted assessments (25% each): Listening, Speaking, Reading, and Writing.
keyTopics: Identity and Culture: Youth, Festivals & Digital Technology
Local Area, Holiday and Travel across the Hispanic World
School, Future Studies, Employment & Global Issues

title: A-Level Fine Art
entryRequirements: Minimum Grade 6 in GCSE Art & Design (or portfolio interview demonstrating technical drawing and media experimentation).
description: An ambitious studio practice course covering drawing, oil painting, printmaking, sculpture, and mixed media installation. Students hold an end-of-year public exhibition in our Bloomsbury college gallery.

teacher.name: Ms. Rowena Blake
teacher.role: Head of Fine Art & Visual Culture
teacher.credentials: MFA Fine Art (Slade School of Fine Art, UCL), Royal Academy Schools

assessmentMethod: Component 1: Personal Investigation with 3,000-word contextual essay (60%); Component 2: Externally Set Assignment with 15-hour practical exam (40%).
keyTopics: Observational Drawing, Oil and Acrylic Painting Mastery
Printmaking, Etching, Screen Printing & Digital Media
Contextual Art History and Critical Visual Analysis
Solo Portfolio Preparation & Degree Show Curation
